body.statement: For every factual cell \(v\) and raw explicit unnested conjunction \(\gamma\), first compute \(\gamma^{\circ}=\mathsf N(\gamma)\) and its normalized context set \(\mathcal H\), and let \(h=|\mathcal H|\). Set \(r=1\), \(\gamma_1^{\circ}=\gamma^{\circ}\), \(c_1=1\), and \(g=g_{\gamma^{\circ}}\), where \(g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f)=\mathbf 1\{\gamma^{\circ}(f)\}\). Under this coefficient convention, \(\ell_g(v)=\min_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f)\), \(u_g(v)=\max_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f)\), \(L_g(p)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal X}p(v)\ell_g(v)\), and \(U_g(p)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal X}p(v)u_g(v)\). The compiler \(\mathsf C_1\) decides whether some \(f\in F_v\) satisfies \(\gamma^{\circ}\), and returns a sparse witness when one exists, in \(B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) time including normalization. A false self-intervention truth constant produced by \(\mathsf N\) makes the conjunction identically false. Otherwise a retained atom \(V_{i,I}=y\) is true for every \(f\in F_v\) if and only if \( |\mathcal D_i|=1\), or \(I\) agrees with \(v\) and \(v_i=y\); hence the conjunction's false bit is decided by a linear scan of normalized constants and retained atoms. By the canonical-carrier equivalence, the endpoints \(L_g(p)\) and \(U_g(p)\) are sharp over the standard parent-subset class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and total sparse-input time is \(sB_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) after charging dense or sparse input reading. On the same order-only class and conjunction target, these endpoints equal those of Rossetto--Antonucci, while the sparse-input construction strictly replaces their completed-signature alphabet-product quotient by an \(h\)-parameter transition system.
body.justification: The theorem gives an exact sharp-bound routine whose exponential factor depends on the normalized world count rather than alphabet cardinality.
body.gap: Rossetto--Antonucci's exact lifted program retains an alphabet-product optimization space; this theorem is a strict computational tightening on the same order-only model and conjunction target.
body.consumer: Sharp probabilities of necessity, sufficiency, and other explicit multi-world conjunctions become tractable when the normalized number of contexts is small even with many-valued variables.
body.proof_tex:
By \texttt{lem:query-normalization}, computing \(\gamma^{\circ}=\mathsf N(\gamma)\) costs \(O(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) and preserves its truth for every response system. Under \(r=1\), \(c_1=1\), the definition of the joint truth support specializes to
\[
 A_v=\{(g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f)):f\in F_v\}\subseteq\{0,1\}.
\]
Consequently \texttt{def:cell-labels} gives
\[
 \ell_g(v)=\min_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f),
 \qquad
 u_g(v)=\max_{f\in F_v}g_{\gamma^{\circ}}(f).
 \tag{5}
\]
The fibre \(F_v\) is nonempty: prescribe \(f_i(v_{<i})=v_i\) at every coordinate and use an arbitrary value from the nonempty alphabet on every other row.

The dynamic program begins with the unique partition of \(\mathcal H\) at layer zero, applies \(\mathsf C_1\)'s representative transitions, and merges equal successor partitions. Induction over coordinates using \texttt{lem:representative-transition} proves that its states are exactly the partitions induced by feasible partial response systems satisfying all factual and conjunction pins already encountered. Soundness follows because every retained representative is realized by a response row; completeness follows because every concrete legal output has a retained representative with the same successor partition and future support. Hence a terminal accepting state exists if and only if some \(f\in F_v\) satisfies \(\gamma^{\circ}\).

Store a predecessor state and selected representative column on the first edge reaching each state. When a state has several concrete histories, \texttt{thm:partition-continuation} permits the selected successor column to be realized from the stored representative history as well. Backtracking an accepting terminal state therefore produces a legal column path. Sparse-response completion then returns \(\widehat f\in F_v\) with at most \(kh\) stored rows and default \(v_i\) at coordinate \(i\).

There are at most \(B_h\) partition states per layer. The corrected exact transition count is at most \(3^{h/3}\), so the total work is
\[
 B_h3^{h/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})
 =3^{1/3}B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]
The constant \(3^{1/3}\), the \(k\) layers, alphabet scans, pin checks, canonical partition encodings, and traceback are absorbed in the displayed polynomial factor. Thus the runtime has exactly the form claimed in the theorem, including when \(h=0\).

We next derive the false bit. Let \(A=\{V_{i,I}=y\}\) be a retained atom. Then \(i\notin\operatorname{dom}(I)\), and every intervention coordinate is below \(i\). We claim
\[
 \bigl(\forall f\in F_v:\ E(f,I)_i=y\bigr)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal D_i|=1
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \bigl(I(t)=v_t\text{ for every }t\in\operatorname{dom}(I)\text{ and }v_i=y\bigr).
 \tag{6}
\]
If \(|\mathcal D_i|=1\), input validity forces \(y\) to be the unique value. If \(I\) agrees with \(v\), ordered induction below \(i\) gives \(E(f,I)_{<i}=v_{<i}\) for every \(f\in F_v\), and then \(E(f,I)_i=f_i(v_{<i})=v_i=y\). This proves the reverse implication.

For the forward implication, suppose \(|\mathcal D_i|>1\). If \(I\) agrees with \(v\) but \(v_i\neq y\), every member of \(F_v\) falsifies the atom. If \(I\) disagrees with \(v\), its first disagreeing intervention coordinate makes the complete \(I\)-world prefix differ permanently from the factual complete prefix. Choose \(z\in\mathcal D_i\setminus\{y\}\), prescribe the factual rows \(f_t(v_{<t})=v_t\), prescribe arbitrary consistent rows along the distinct \(I\)-world prefix through \(i-1\), and set
\[
 f_i(E(f,I)_{<i})=z,
 \qquad
 f_i(v_{<i})=v_i.
\]
The two arguments of \(f_i\) are distinct, so the prescriptions are consistent. Complete all other rows by defaults. The resulting member of \(F_v\) falsifies the atom, proving (6).

A false truth constant produced by normalization makes the entire conjunction false. Otherwise, if every retained atom satisfies the right side of (6), every response system in \(F_v\) satisfies the conjunction, so \(\ell_g(v)=1\). If some atom fails that condition, the response system just constructed falsifies that atom and hence the conjunction, so \(\ell_g(v)=0\). A linear scan of constants and retained atoms therefore decides the false bit. This argument needs one witness falsifying one atom, not one witness simultaneously falsifying all atoms. The empty conjunction has both labels equal to one, and the true bit is the accepting-state decision already proved.

For any compatible canonical law \(\mu\), the disjoint fibres \((F_v)_{v\in\mathcal X}\), observational compatibility, and (5) give
\[
 \theta_g
 =\sum_{v\in\mathcal X}\sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)g(f),
 \qquad
 \sum_{f\in F_v}\mu(f)=p(v),
 \qquad
 \ell_g(v)\leq g(f)\leq u_g(v).
\]
Since \(\mu(f)\geq0\), summation yields
\[
 L_g(p)\leq\theta_g\leq U_g(p).
 \tag{7}
\]
For every positive-mass cell, choose a minimizing response system and assign it exogenous mass \(p(v)\); this gives a compatible law attaining \(L_g(p)\). Choosing maximizers gives one attaining \(U_g(p)\). Zero-mass cells require no atom. Convex mixtures of the endpoint laws preserve \(p\) and fill the interval. Proposition~\texttt{prop:canonical-carrier-equivalence} transfers these sharp endpoints to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\).

Lemma~\texttt{lem:rossetto-antonucci-order-lp-interface} says that Rossetto--Antonucci's canonical response-signature program has the sharp extrema over this same order-only class and observational law. Since (7) and its attaining constructions characterize those extrema, the endpoint values coincide. Their cited interface begins with completed predecessor response signatures and then quotients by observational-cell and query-truth evaluations. The present construction instead generates only reachable partitions for the requested cells and never constructs a completed signature; its exponential indices are \(B_h\) and \(3^{(h-1)/3}\), while alphabet processing is a charged polynomial scan. This establishes the stated representational replacement.

On a sparse input, the procedure is run only for the \(s\) explicitly listed positive-mass cells, giving
\[
 sB_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
\]
For a dense input, reading every supplied cell is already included in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\). No omitted sample cell is treated as a structural zero.
